Et il ne s’agit pas que de luttes, mais: And it's not just about struggles, but about everything that makes her the person she is.
Le Gala Dynastie souligne chaque année l: Every year, the Gala Dynastie honours the contributions of Black public figures from a range of fields. The five finalists in the Engaged Web Personality of the Year category speak out online to make their ideas heard. We talked to those who express themselves loud and clear on our screens.
« Je n’ai rien à gagner », souligne Jess: “I have nothing to gain,” says Jessica Prudencio with a laugh, referring to the stands she takes. At first, the content creator simply wanted to share her lived experience. “I started speaking up naturally, from the experiences I was living personally, just by existing as a fat Black woman.” Social media is what allowed her to create this space to express herself.
En bâtissant sa plateforme, elle se rend: As she built her platform, she realized how important a project like this is: making heard those who are too often absent from the dominant discourse. “The experiences and voices of people who are marginalized deserve to be heard,” she says. And it's not just about struggles, but about everything that makes her the person she is. Fashion, food, beauty – Jessica shares her captivating, colourful world on Instagram. She also co-hosts a podcast, Where We At, dedicated to Indigenous, Black and people of colour (BIPOC). She doesn't hesitate to speak out on social issues, such as fatphobia and racism, on all of her platforms. Online, followers regularly take the opportunity to contact Jessica directly, something she laments. Yet they have all the tools at their disposal to educate themselves.
« Il y a beaucoup de paresse intellectue: “There's a lot of intellectual laziness with social media,” she believes. “I'm not here to do the work for them,” says the woman, who has no qualms about not responding to inquisitive requests.
« Mon milieu est très blanc », dit-elle: “My circle is very white,” she says of her clients, followers and collaborators. “It warms my heart to have the recognition of the Black community,” the young woman adds. “We're constantly ‘invisibilized,’” she says of the place of BIPOC people in the media landscape. “Nobody wants to hear us speak, nobody wants to see us.” The trend is slowly reversing, but the battle is far from won. “Things will change the day we're truly given a voice,” she declares. “When we have our own platforms, our own media, and we can say what we want without being afraid of reprisals.”
Marcus Troy vit également de ses passion: Marcus Troy also lives off his passions. An entrepreneur, he owns a creative agency and wears many hats. His experience has led him, too, to be critical of the industry in which he works. “People who don't look like us tell us what's cool in our culture and our ideas, and tell us what we should see or feel. We should be hearing more diverse opinions and voices, from Black people in particular, because they're the most influential group of people in the world,” he believes. “It's just that we don't get the same respect.”
Son entreprise ne dépend pas des réseaux: His company doesn't depend on social media, but the web remains a tool that lets him share the projects he's working on and the things close to his heart.
« S’il y a une chose dont les oppresseur: “If there's one thing the oppressors didn't take into account, it's the Internet,” he says. “The Internet has shown a lot of things, it has given people the ability to express themselves.” Marcus believes the web also offers an opportunity to demand accountability, to hold institutions and companies responsible for their actions.
Bien qu’il s’agisse pour lui avant tout: Although he sees it first and foremost as a creative tool, the entrepreneur doesn't hold back from speaking out when he feels the need. “When something happens, I speak up on the subjects that matter to me and my community. I try to be present with my voice.”
L’humoriste Renzel Dashington en était à: Comedian Renzel Dashington was at the second performance of his first one-man show, 10, when the pandemic abruptly forced him to suspend his shows. In response to the lockdown, he made his first live video on social media last March.
Un an plus tard, on compte plus d’une ce: A year later, there are more than a hundred live episodes, each an hour long and racking up thousands of views. While his main goal is to entertain, Renzel nevertheless sparks plenty of discussion among members of his audience. “I'm talking to a room full of Black people who want to hear the things we're all talking about,” he says. His brand of humour lends itself well to social commentary. “We're going to laugh a lot about things that aren't important, because that's also part of being Black.
On va également parler de choses sérieus: We're also going to talk about serious things and subjects that concern us, that have an impact on our lives.” He is alone in front of the camera, and the free-flowing style of live videos lets him work out his acting muscle. “Comedy's job is to make people laugh, yes, but what has the most effect is when the comedian gives you a chance to see something you already know in a different light,” the artist believes.
Dans ses vidéos, la section commentaires: In his videos, the comments section is lively from start to finish, with people participating enormously. “I'm happy to be the lubricant, the facilitator of the conversations we wanted to have,” the comedian says. He compares himself to a neighbour who simply wants to be around his own people and break the isolation of community members. The comedian's online presence has got him noticed on the cultural scene, notably by his peers. Despite this, he doesn't believe his future lies in traditional media, in part because what he says doesn't please their audiences.
« On va m’entendre dire des choses qu’il: “You'll hear me say things they don't want to hear. Listeners told me I wasn't helping the anti-racist cause,” he laments, referring to a segment on 98.5 FM. “I don't think they'd hire me. If it were possible, they would have done it already.” He prefers to stay free and, above all, to be where his audience is.
Petrona Joseph attire la confidence : en: Petrona Joseph draws out confidences: hearing her story, you immediately want to tell her yours. “I'm a blogger and a mental health spokesperson,” she says over the phone. “Did I intend to become one? No!” she exclaims with a laugh. A linguist by training, she decided to return to her first love – writing – changing careers after finding success in business development for luxury brands. “I wasn't accepted in the business world,” she says of her experience as a Black woman.
Récemment, une dépression l’a forcée à r: Recently, depression forced her to slow down her activities. She decided to speak about the illness on her platform. “I talked a lot about my struggle this year,” she says. “And I truly believe it's my life's purpose,” she adds of this new turn. Petrona's story resonated enormously with the public. Many of her followers saw themselves in her. In this way, the influencer was able to build connections and reach many women. Communicating with them regularly, she supports them on their journey.
« La santé mentale est stigmatisée dans: “Mental health is stigmatized in Black communities,” she believes. Petrona is currently finishing a book on the subject, born of the questions people send her. She is now regularly invited to share her experience all over, online, but also on radio and television. The author is no stranger to TV sets, having previously hosted the local fashion segment on Breakfast Television.
Si le web a façonné sa carrière, elle pe: Although the web shaped her career, she still thinks she could have carved out a place to tell her story in traditional media. It was first by giving advice that Thierry Lindor began speaking out on social media.
« J’ai toujours été entrepreneur, mais j: “I've always been an entrepreneur, but I've got a big mouth, actually,” exclaims the engaged citizen, who is also a UN delegate. His commentary mostly concerns real estate and entrepreneurship, his fields of expertise. He also appears regularly on television as a specialist in these areas, a privilege he attributes to being a man and to colourism. “Around 2018, I started to understand the power of social media,” he says. He was sharing his TV appearances online at the time and noticed that a dialogue was forming in the community.
« Très rapidement, j’ai compris que je d: “Very quickly, I understood that I had to migrate from a platform that was offered to me sporadically to one that I could create,” he explains.
Depuis quelques années, il est beaucoup: For the past few years, he has been much more active on social media, where he talks about financial literacy, property ownership, but also current events. “What gives me hope is that my kids will have tremendous opportunities, because non-traditional media and digital platforms are growing.”
C’est peut-être bien la voie de l’avenir: It may well be the path of the future for those we hear from less, but who have so much to say.
